suggestions.quote: You love Mom; Sent is nearly empty.
suggestions.fix: Don't narrate the love. Let the sliver of mom's bar in Sent carry it, and say one dry, hushed line over it: "Sent. Mom's bar. A sliver."

suggestions.quote: her seat at the chai stall is empty, and her row stopped on a day you can't name
suggestions.fix: Don't narrate what the empty seat and the dark row already show. Speak only the gap, in a hushed fragment: "Her stool. Empty. Since... when?"

suggestions.quote: Your best photo: three hundred likes, four coins.
suggestions.fix: Add the gap as an amused, deadpan beat with the number repeated: "Three hundred likes. Four coins. Four." Keep the digits out of the spoken line; the story numbers are already written as words, so it needs no claims row.

suggestions.quote: people guess far more of a room noticed them than did
suggestions.fix: This reads like an essay line. Make it spoken and one number: "You'd guess half the carriage looked. Tell me, how many did? Hardly anyone." Give the spoken form for say.yaml, e.g. "nineteen percent" if G2 confirms the figure, never "19%". The line lands on you, in a curious tone.
Give say.yaml the spoken form "two in the morning". Direct the title question in a curious, slightly amused tone, and give Arthur a breath after "paid you?" so the thumbnail moment lands first.

keep.quote: Coins are care. At least now you can count it
